title: Appel d’offres – Fourniture de denrées alimentaires pour la Résidence Visagno – Années 2027-2028
description:
Objet : Appel d’offres – Fourniture de denrées alimentaires pour la Résidence Visagno – Années 2027-2028

Madame, Monsieur,

Vous trouverez en annexe le cahier des charges ainsi que le formulaire d’offre relatifs à la fourniture de denrées alimentaires destinées à l’établissement médico-social « Résidence Visagno » pour les années 2027 et 2028.

La procédure est soumise à l’Accord intercantonal sur les marchés publics (AIMP) du 25 novembre 1994 / 15 mars 2001 et à ses dispositions complémentaires, à la Loi sur les marchés publics (LMP) du 20 février 2001 ainsi qu’à son règlement d’application (RLMP/AIMP) et à leurs mises à jour.

Les principales informations relatives à la procédure sont les suivantes :

  • Questions relatives à l’appel d’offres : elles doivent être adressées exclusivement par courrier électronique à l’adresse amministrazione@residenzavisagno.ch, au plus tard le 24 novembre 2026. Les questions reçues après cette date ne seront pas prises en considération.
  • Réponses aux questions : les réponses seront communiquées anonymement par courrier électronique à l’ensemble des soumissionnaires. Une confirmation de réception devra être transmise à la Résidence Visagno, conformément à l’art. 12, al. 2 RLMP/AIMP.
  • Remise des offres : le formulaire d’offre, accompagné de la liste des prix correspondante, doit être remis en format papier ainsi qu’en format numérique sur une clé USB.
  • Qualité des produits : les denrées alimentaires faisant l’objet du présent appel d’offres sont destinées à la préparation des repas des résidents de l’établissement. Les soumissionnaires sont responsables de la qualité des produits proposés ainsi que du respect des normes légales en vigueur.
  • Délai de remise des offres : l’offre doit parvenir à la Résidence Visagno au plus tard le 22 décembre 2026 à 14h00. Le cachet postal ne fait pas foi.
  • Identification de l’enveloppe : l’enveloppe contenant l’offre doit porter impérativement la mention suivante : « Ne pas ouvrir – Appel d’offres denrées alimentaires Résidence Visagno 2027-2028 ».
  • Ouverture des offres : elle aura lieu immédiatement après l’expiration du délai de remise, dans les locaux de la Résidence Visagno. Le procès-verbal d’ouverture mentionnera uniquement le nom des soumissionnaires. En principe, l’adjudication pourra être effectuée par produit individuel ou par module complet, conformément à l’art. 10 des prescriptions et conditions.
  • Lieu de livraison : l’ensemble des denrées alimentaires devra être livré à la Résidence Visagno, à Claro.

Des exemplaires supplémentaires du cahier des charges peuvent être obtenus auprès de l’administration, à l’adresse suivante : amministrazione@residenzavisagno.ch.

En cas de désintérêt pour la présente procédure, nous vous prions de bien vouloir nous en informer par écrit ou par courrier électronique avant l’échéance du délai de remise des offres.

Nous attirons votre attention sur les dispositions de l’art. 42 RLMP/AIMP. À titre d’exemple, les offres remises hors délai ou dont l’enveloppe ne comporte pas la mention prescrite seront exclues de la procédure. Par ailleurs, conformément à l’art. 39, al. 5 RLMP, les demandes de prolongation des délais de paiement relatifs aux charges sociales et aux impôts ne sont pas admises.

Nous vous remercions de l’intérêt porté à notre appel d’offres et vous adressons, Madame, Monsieur, nos salutations distinguées.

Résidence Visagno

Administration

title: APN_Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3, CFB Borden ON
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Construction of Training Quarters Buildings 2 and 3 CFB Borden, Ontario (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at CFB Borden, Ontario. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following 2-Step (Step 1: Request for Expression of Interest, Step 2: Tender Phase) solicitation will proceed as noted below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN Number: 88280 Approximate Estimate: $168 million for both buildings Anticipated Posting Step 1: January 2027 Anticipated Posting Step 2: February 2027 Description: The project comprises the construction of two new five-storey training quarters buildings at CFB Borden, Ontario. The buildings will use a site-adapted design based on the existing Training Quarters Building S-166. The anticipated work includes building construction, mechanical and electrical systems, associated site development and connections to site services. The design will incorporate site-specific requirements and lessons learned from the existing building.  3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer or proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security screening requirement for each construction contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors or consultants early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors or consultants that intend to submit a tender or a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers or proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors or consultants are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors or consultants to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor or consultant: Have submitted a response to the Step 1: RFEOI, have submitted a Sponsorship application prior to the date of publication of the Step 2: Tender Phase, meet all material requirements of the sponsorship application package by the closing date of the Step 2: Tender Phase, and Have submitted a tender to the Step 2: Tender Phase. DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors or Consultants that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer or proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Victor Shekofteh Contract Coordinator Defence Construction Canada 249-535-4651 victor.shekofteh@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer or proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer or proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

Phase 2: • The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. • The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report). • Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: No travel required. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice. The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices. Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight. Details: Essential (mandatory) Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required. 2. Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization. 2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks). 2B. Demonstrate how governance information can be collected, aggregated and maintained across multiple systems through APIs, connectors and data exchange mechanisms. 2C. Leverage open standards and documented interfaces to reduce dependency on proprietary technologies enabling interoperability across diverse enterprise environments. 3. Demonstrate how administrative, support and access to governance information and data can be restricted, monitored and controlled in accordance with the GoC requirements. 3A. Enable organizations to define and manage data residency requirements, retention, access and deletion of policies and information without vendor intervention. 4. Enable assessment and reassessment of registered AI systems applicable AI governance requirements, policies, standards, directives while supporting reassessment when governance requirements, assessment frameworks are added modified, replaced or retired. The solution must demonstrate the ability to translate AI governance requirements into traceable controls assess whether applicable controls have been satisfied and identify non-conformities. 4A. Enable authorized users to add, modify, version, replace or retire governance requirements and assessment frameworks to individual AI systems or groups. Demonstrate compliance assessment at minimum against the Policy on Service and Digital, Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessment, AI Strategy and AI ethics and responsibilities. 4B. Demonstrate the ability to add, modify, version, replace and retire governance requirements, controls and assessment criteria, and assign them to individual AI systems or groups of AI systems. while supporting the application of different assessment criteria to different AI systems based on their intended use, risk profile or governance requirements Offerors are encouraged to prove extensibility to additional internationally recognized governance frameworks and standards, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the EU Act. 4C. Generate human-readable explanations of assessment and reassessment results. Each finding must identify the applicable requirement, evidence considered, assessment result and confidence score or a certainty measure. user. 4D. Collect, link, and retain assurance artefacts including control mapping, assessment records, evidence references, approvals, exceptions, attestations, remediation actions and audit histories. Competitive Procurement Strategy: Lowest cost Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: No Nature of Requirements: Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector THIS REQUEST IS RESERVED FOR HOLDERS OF SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT # E60PV-19EQUI ONLY, FOR THE PURCHASE OF LABORATORY AND SCIENTIFIC EQUIPMENT, PARTS AND ACCESSORIES, SERVICES AND SUPPLIES. Only Suppliers currently pre-qualified on Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI have been invited to bid. As a requirement of the Supply Arrangement, this notice is published on Government Electronic Tendering Service (GETS) for a period of 40 calendar days. The closing date published on this notice identifies how long the notice will be published. For the closing date of any solicitation under the supply arrangement, invited suppliers should refer to the solicitation documents. Suppliers that do not have a Supply Arrangement for the supply of Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies with Public Works and Government Services Canada, cannot submit a bid. Any bids received from suppliers not pre-qualified on the Supply Arrangement will not be evaluated. Suppliers may qualify under Supply Arrangement E60PV-19EQUI for Laboratory and Scientific Equipment, Parts and Accessories, Services and Supplies, at any time. Interested suppliers should download solicitation document E60PV-19EQUI/D from CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba) and submit a response as per the requirements of the Request for Supply Arrangement. Item : Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) Detector Quantity: 1 The mandatory technical criteria are: # MANDATORY TECHNICAL CRITERIA M1 Must be capable of being installed on a TESCAN Mira3 XMH model scanning electron microscope M2 Must come equipped with a CMOS sensor, a phosphor screen, and fibre-optic coupling M3 Must be capable of collecting EBSD patterns with image sizes up to 1244x1024 M4 Must have pattern acquisition speeds of up to 5700 patterns per second at 156x128 resolution M5 Must allow analyses at beam currents as low as 400 pA and accelerating voltages as low as 5kV M6 Must be capable of angular resolution up to 0.05 degrees M7 Must have motorized screen elevation control and insertion/retraction control M8 Must come equipped with a 5 diode forescatter diode (FSD) array for orientation contrast, topographic contrast, and atomic number contrast imaging M9 Must come with a Windows PC workstation installed with software for data acquisition and processing. M10 Must be capable of simultaneous EDS/EBSD mapping with an X-Max 80 model EDS detector, permitting refined phase identification using sample chemistry. Note: The X-Max 80 is the exact model of EDS detector currently installed in the laboratory. We rely on a function where simultaneously collected EDS data is used to aid in the correct identification of crystallographically similar phases during automated EBSD analyses, and therefore any new EBSD detector must be compatible with our X-Max 80.

title: Albania – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Preparation of audits, detailed design, tender documents, supervision of civil works for the implementation of energy efficiency measures in local public buildings across all four municipalities
description: This Contract covers the preparation of investment-ready documentation for 50 pre-selected local public buildings in the municipalities of Berat, Shkodër, Korçë and Përmet, including offices, kindergartens, libraries, and social and cultural centres. The Assignment includes the preparation of energy audits, detailed technical designs, building permit documentation, Bills of Quantities, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and PRAG-compliant tender documentation. All 50 buildings will be assessed and prioritised in accordance with DCM No. 468/2024 . Based on this prioritisation, buildings with a total gross floor area of at least 22,000 m² will be selected for the implementation of energy-efficiency measures under a subsequent Works Contract. The Contract also includes the supervision of the civil works implemented in the selected buildings. The Service Contract is structured in two phases, comprising a total of 60 months of service provision, with a 12-month interim period between the two phases. Phase 1, lasting 24 months, covers the energy audit, preparation of the detailed technical design and preparation of the tender dossier for the Works Contract. This phase will be followed by a 12-month interim period, during which the procurement procedure for the Works Contract is expected to take place and no services will be required under the Service Contract. Phase 2, lasting 36 months, will cover the supervision and monitoring of the Works, commencing upon the start of the Works Contract.

title: Table-Top Free Space Measuring System - USDA-ARS Auburn AL
description: This is a Sources Sought notice Only. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only as part of USDA ARS market research and does not itself constitute an RFQ. This requirement is covered under NAICS code 334516 � Analytical Laboratory Instrument Manufacturing. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified sources; Small Businesses; HUBZone small business; service-disabled, veteran-owned small business; 8(a) small business; veteran-owned small business; woman-owned small business; or small disadvantaged businesses; Responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. The USDA-ARS National Soil Dynamics laboratory (NSDL) is in need of a specialized microwave instrument which enables the user to measure reflection and transmission data while not touching nor destroying (NDE) the sample. The following are the specification required for this instrument. 1. Small table-top frame for transmission and reflection measurements. 2. The frame with two probes at the proper alignment and distance for optimal measurements and has a versatile sample holder to allow for multiple specimen types and sizes. 3. The frame with two probes for a frequency range of at least 2.5 GHz to 20 GHz. 4. At least one pair of SMA cables designed for use up to at least 25 GHz. 5. Two probes should be able to be connected to a VNA. 6. Software for VNA that calculates the S-parameters. 7. Free Space Measurement Methods to characterize materials. 8. Enables the user to measure reflection and transmission of electromagnet waves data while not touching nor destroying (NDE) the sample The Government does not intend to make an award based on responses to this inquiry. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Capability Statement All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Business concerns that possess the capabilities necessary to undertake this work should submit complete documentation of their capabilities to the Contracting Officer. Capability statements shall include the Contractors contact point to discuss their response. The capability statement should include: 1) Acknowledgement that they are able to provide the subject supplies/services being requested; 2) Interested vendors should identify their size standards in accordance with the Small Business Administration; 3) At least three previous requirements that are similar to the requirement include a discussion of the Contract type, delivery method, duration, etc.; 4) Any other information considered relevant to this requirement; and 5) The government requests that no proprietary, classified, confidential, or sensitive information should be included in the response. Any vendor responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine their qualifications to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. After review of the responses received, a combined synopsis/solicitation may be published on sam.gov depending on the responses received. All responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be received by the notice�s POC by the deadline in order to be considered. Responses may not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Inquiry. Do not submit pricing information in response to this Request.

title: Office of Hazardous Materials Safety Research Initiative � FY2026 BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA)
description: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. Full eligibility, formatting, and submission instructions are detailed in the solicitation document attached to this notice.

INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. Interested parties may respond regardless of whether they attended the event. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. Respondents should address the capability areas and information requested in this RFI without assuming any relationship to that program�s requirements, acquisition approach, funding, schedule, or procurement quantities. BACKGROUND Simulation-based training has the potential to enhance operator proficiency, improve training availability, increase training throughput, reduce operational risk, and provide realistic Mission Planning and Mission Rehearsal capabilities for Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. These capabilities may enable operators to safely practice in realistic and challenging operational and threat environments, emergency procedures, and degraded system behaviors that may be impractical, unsafe, or cost-prohibitive to execute using live aircraft. Simulation-based training may also reduce operational impacts associated with range availability, airspace restrictions, spectrum congestion, weather delays, aircraft maintenance requirements, and logistical constraints while supporting standardized, repeatable, and scalable training across multiple UAS platforms. The Government seeks to understand current industry capabilities, technology maturity, innovative approaches, best practices, and limitations relevant to these objectives. MARKET RESEARCH PROCESS This RFI represents the white-paper phase of Air PMO's market research effort. The Government may use information received to support capability development, requirements refinement, acquisition planning, evaluation of commercially available and emerging solutions, and potential procurement strategies. Following review of submitted white papers, the Government may invite selected respondents to participate in follow-up discussions or technical demonstrations to further assess the maturity, suitability, and applicability of proposed solutions. Selection for, or participation in, a follow-up activity does not constitute a competitive range determination, source-selection decision, commitment to procure, or preference for any future acquisition. Any invitation and associated instructions will be issued separately. The Government may elect not to conduct follow-up activities and is not obligated to provide feedback to respondents. INFORMATION REQUESTED Respondents should provide a concise white paper describing how their solution addresses the capability areas in this RFI. Responses should identify current capabilities separately from planned, developmental, or partner-provided capabilities. At a minimum, the white paper should address the following: Company profile, business size and socioeconomic status, Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and primary point(s) of contact. Executive summary of the proposed solution and the operational or training problem it addresses. Description of the complete solution, including software, hardware, peripherals, hosting or deployment model, licensing, and any Government-furnished equipment or services required. A capability cross-reference identifying each applicable Capability Area of Interest as currently available, configurable, developmental, not available, or provided by a third party. For developmental capabilities, identify the anticipated availability date and key dependencies. Supported Group 1 and Group 2 UAS platforms, flight models, ground control stations, hand controllers, payloads, mission-planning tools, and training environments, including the approach and estimated effort to add new aircraft or configurations. Technical maturity and commercial availability, including Technology Readiness Level or equivalent maturity evidence, operational use, customer base, relevant contracts, and available test or performance data. System architecture, interfaces, data formats, application programming interfaces, standards, modularity, and approach to integration with Government or third-party systems. Training-management, instructor, evaluation, after-action review, records-management, and qualification-management functionality. Cybersecurity, identity and access management, data protection, software-update, cloud or on-premises deployment, and authority-to-operate status or experience, as applicable. NDAA and supply-chain compliance status, including identification of any noncompliant components, planned remediation, dependencies, or assumptions. title: TURBO SUPERCHARGER / NSN 2950-01-714-4392 / JOINT LIGHT TACTICAL VEHICLE
description: An Unrestricted solicitation will be issued to establish an Indefinite Quantity Contract (IQC) for NSN 2950-01-714-4392, a TURBO SUPERCHARGER. The award will be for a 5-year base period. The Estimated Annual Quantity (EAQ) is 40 EACH. Production units will be FOB: Destination; Inspection /Acceptance: Destination. Item is not critical nor deemed a Critical Safety Item. Surge does not apply. The proposed contract action is for supplies for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one or a limited number of sources under the authority of FAR 6.302. The sole approved source is Banks Technologies (CAGE 7PMZ4) in accordance with part number 12645. DLA Weapons Support - Richmond does NOT possess complete technical data on this part. There are no other approved sources at this time. Any other interested contractor would have to submit a Source Approval Request (SAR) package for approval to be added as a source by the assigned ESA. Interested persons may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all proposals received within forty-five days after date of publication of this synopsis will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete with this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, in its solicitation for the described supplies. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice. In order to receive an award, regardless of dollar value, contractors must be registered in the System For Award Management (sam.gov). The final contract award decision may be based upon a combination of price, past performance and other evaluation factors as described in the solicitation. The estimated solicitation issue date is 11/20/2026. A copy of the solicitation will be available via DIBBS at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil/ on the issue date cited in the RFP. Choose the RFP you wish to download. RFPs are in portable document format (PDF). To download and view these documents you will need the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of this solicitation will not be available to requesters.

title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. Email your questions to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov. Notice of Intent to Propose Any interested party intending to submit a proposal must submit a "Notice of Intent to Propose" as described in the Business Opportunity and Proposal Instructions, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on November 23, 2026. Submission of Electronic Proposal The NPS is ONLY accepting electronic proposals in response to this prospectus. Any proposal must be received electronically, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on December 22, 2026, in the format outlined in the Proposal Instructions, to be evaluated for award of the new concession contract. Contact List The prospectus is available on the NPS Commercial Services website (link provided below). If you choose to retrieve a copy of the prospectus, please notify Mark Juretschke at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov so you are placed on the mailing list to receive notifications of any future modifications or correspondence.

title: Beach Renourishment, Kennedy Space Center, Brevard County, Florida
description: This announcement constitutes a Source Sought Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking interest from prospective offerors for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 award of the aforementioned project. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gauge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of the Construction and Dredging Communities, to include Small Businesses, as the Government must ensure there is adequate competition amongst the potential pool of responsible contractors. The notice is also soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for this large-scale construction project exceeding $35,000,000. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said notice or any follow-up information requested. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of an Invitation For Bid (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said sources sought notice or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The proposed project work will consist of nourishing approximately 4.1 miles shoreline along Kennedy Space Center between FDEP Range Monuments V-366 and V-386 in Brevard County, Florida. The project includes dredging approximately 2.5 million cubic yards (MCY) of material for construction of a beach berm and dune. Beach compatible sand for the project may be dredged from up to three (3) offshore borrow areas. Chester Shoals I is located east of Cape Canaveral in State waters and is centered approximately 1.7 miles offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Kennedy Shoals and Hetzel Shoals are located east of Cape Canaveral in Federal waters and are centered approximately 4.5 miles and 10 miles, respectively, offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Project work also includes, but is not limited to, beach tilling, turbidity monitoring, environmental species monitoring, and Munitions and Explosive of Concern (MEC) support. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 280 calendar days after issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP), including 60 calendar days to commence work. Magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The NAICS Code is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD SIZE IS $45,000,000.00. Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about June 1, 2027 and the anticipated bid opening day is on or about July 1, 2027. The official Synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on the SAM.gov Contracting Opportunities Website: www.sam.gov. title: Digital Talking Book Machines - Library of Congress
description: Amendment 2: Changes the PPQ. - - - Solicitation Amendment -0001 answers Offeror questions. Please see 030ADV27R0001 -0001, Attachment J-6, and revised Attachment J-1. - - - This public notice is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12 and utilizing FAR Part 15 procedures. The solicitation is being released as an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract competition. This contract shall include two performance areas to encompass all aspects of procuring new Digital Talking Book Machines and maintaining the new and existing stock at the Library. Performance Area 1 (PA1): DTBM DA2 Production, Parts, and Support This PA includes DA2 units, warranties, spare parts, software development, and other requirements described in Section C. NLS requires Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) version DA2 units in quantities sufficient to continue distribution to all audio readers enrolled in the program and maintain a reasonable stock to allow timely replacement of devices in the field to facilitate service, repair, or maintenance of removed devices. NLS requires support for those units including spare parts, software development, and warranty repairs. Performance Area 2 (PA2): Existing Device Support, Incumbent This PA includes proprietary spare parts and software development as described in Section C. NLS also requires repair and support services for the existing incumbent-manufactured NLS DTBM DA2 units (approximately 63,000). This includes spare parts and platform sprints to ensure the units remain safe, functional, and accessible so that the Library�s patrons have the fullest access to materials in the NLS collection. Please see all attachments for the full details of this requirement and instructions for submitting a proposal. Questions are due by 5:00pm eastern time, September 14, 2026. Proposals are due by 5:00pm eastern time, October 5, 2026.

title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – DAS SURF Cumulus Professional Services 2023
description: De toekomst van de ICT en bijbehorende dienstverlening voor onderwijs- en onderzoek ligt volgens SURF én de leden voor een belangrijk deel in de cloud. De leden (instellingen) willen daarom flexibel gebruik kunnen maken van de cloud en deze combineren met eigen ICT-infrastructuren (hybride infrastructuur). Overgang naar de cloud is in de praktijk geen eenvoudige stap, en voor veel instellingen geldt dat er weinig ervaring mee is opgedaan. Er kunnen daardoor onverwachte uitdagingen ontstaan tijdens de uitvoering van cloud projecten alsook in de beheerfase erna. De initieel beoogde voordelen worden dan niet behaald waardoor afbreukrisico c.q. kapitaalvernietiging kan ontstaan. Om instellingen te ondersteunen bij deze uitdagingen is het dan ook gewenst om SURFcumulus Professional Services via een SURF aanbesteding voor hen beschikbaar te maken. SURF kiest ervoor om dit via een DAS te laten verlopen. De levering van SURFcumulus Professional Services is nadrukkelijk gekoppeld aan de SURFcumulus dienst. Concreet gaat het om uitvoerende, gangbare dienstverlening bedoeld voor cloud implementatie, -migratie en -beheer. Levering gebeurt op basis van vaste prijs en vaste opleverdatum. Een nadere omschrijving van de dienstverleningonderdelen is als volgt: Inrichten van een cloud landing zone, geïntegreerd in de bestaande (hybride) architectuur van een instelling, ten minste omvattend: Account setup: gebaseerd op de administratieve organsiatie, compliance richtlijnen, bestaande omgevingen en structuren van de instelling. Network configuratie: volgens richtlijnen, binnen cloud omgevingen en tussen on-premise en deze cloud omgevingen. Security baseline: identity en access management op basis van SURFconext, bechikbaarheid van gestandaardiseerde, hardened machine images, security policies, network monitoring en log analytics. Automation: gestandaardiseerde inrichting van security, governance, and kostenoptimalisatie. Uitvoeren/ondersteunen van cloud migraties, door middel van: Lift-and-shift migratie scenario: het zonder ingrijpende wijzigingen (deels) verplaatsen van een ICT infrastructuur uit een datacenter naar de cloud. Re-design migratie scenario: het cloud ready maken van (een deel van) een bestaande ICT infrastructuur en/of het implementeren van vervangende, nieuw te bouwen oplossingen waardoor het potentieel van de cloud optimaal benut kan worden. Leveren van cloud managed services in de (hybride) cloud infrastructuur, waaronder bijv.: Operations (accountbeheer, software update management, licentiebeheer, netwerkbeheer, backup & restore, monitoring, platformbeheer) Application management (technisch applicatiebeheer, functioneel applicatiebeheer, gegevensbeheer, applicatie configuratiebeheer) Service support (incident-, problem- & change management, multi vendor coordinatie, tweede en derdelijns support, escalatie afhandeling) Service delivery (service level management, capacity-, cost- en continuity management) Informatie beveiliging en privacy bescherming (detectie, preventie, rapportage, bijsturing). Zie verder het toegevoegde document "Toelatingsleidraad DAS SURFcumulus Professional Services".

title: Germany – Engineering design services for the construction of civil engineering works – Planung Industriebau I Mehrparteienvertrag | Aufbau Kompetenzzentrum KETTE, HIL GmbH
description: Die Bundesrepublik Deutschland beabsichtigt, am Standort St. Wendel die dort ansässigen "HIL Werke" (HIL GmbH) zum Kompetenzzentrum für Kettenfahrzeuge des Heeres (sog. "Kompetenzzentrum KETTE") umzustrukturieren. Im Kompetenzzentrum KETTE sollen zukünftig Kettenfahrzeuge der Bundeswehr gewartet und instandgesetzt werden. Hierzu werden am Standort St. Wendel neue Werks- und Betriebshallen und weitere Gebäude nebst nutzerspezifischen Anlagen - u.a. - Hauptwerkhalle für System- und Baugruppeninstandsetzung sowie Logistik und Servicebereiche (wie z. B. Warenannahme, Ersatzteillager) - Werkhalle für u.a. Turminstandsetzung - Multifunktionsgebäude für u.a. Eingangsbefundung, Ketteninstandsetzung und Ausgangsprüfung - Tankstelle - Systemwaschstraße - Schreinerei/Sattlerei - Motorenprüfstand - Halle für Unterstützungsbereiche - Verwaltungsgebäude (für administrative Arbeiten) - sowie die im Rahmen der gänzlichen Umstrukturierung des Werkareals erforderlichen Außenanlagen (inkl. zugehörige Tiefbauarbeiten und der technischen Infrastruktur) benötigt. Die Projektabwicklung erfolgt mittels der integrierten Projektabwicklung (IPA) unter Anwendung eines Mehrparteienvertrages (MPV).

title: Maximum Length Sequence Phase Encoding for Quantum Sensor Readout
description: Quantum sensors can detect extremely small electromagnetic and magnetic signatures, which makes them powerful tools for geophysical analysis, materials detection, environmental monitoring, and scientific research. Their sensitivity also makes them vulnerable to interference from ambient RF sources, electrical noise, and outdoor or industrial environments. Traditional readout methods attempt to preserve the phase of the sensor or allow it to evolve uniformly, but these approaches can produce ambiguous results or false positives when exposed to strong interference. Los Alamos researchers developed a pseudorandom phase-encoding method that allows a quantum sensor to distinguish true target signals from substantial background noise. By applying a maximum length sequence, also called an msequence, the sensor�s phase is flipped by 180 degrees according to a designed pattern. The resulting measurement is analyzed using correlation against the known sequence, enabling accurate extraction of the intended signal even when conventional methods fail to differentiate between interference and true sensor output. Advantages Improves quantum sensor performance in noisy outdoor and industrial settings Distinguishes true sensor signals from interfering or spurious noise Reduces false positives without added shielding or multichannel detection Integrates into existing measurement protocols with minimal modification Compatible with a range of quantum sensing platforms, including magnetic and electromagnetic systems Technology Description The method embeds a defined sequence of phase inversions into the quantum sensor. Target signals track this imposed pattern because they arise from the controlled experiment, while interfering signals do not. This inherent separation allows correlation-based processing to highlight coherent responses and suppress background noise. Demonstrations using low field nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) show that both traditional CPMG-style readouts and the m-sequence-based readout detect the intended signal under ideal conditions. However, when only interference is present, the traditional readout cannot reliably separate interference from the target signal, while the m-sequence method correctly rejects the interferer. Experimental data also show strong correlation peaks for the encoded measurement and minimal correlation for AM or broadband interferers, confirming the method�s robustness in realistic outdoor and industrial noise environments. Market Applications This phase-encoded readout method supports sensing platforms in which interference can obscure weak or transient signals. Its characteristics make it relevant to a wide range of technologies, including: subsurface imaging and resource characterization in geophysical exploration quantum sensing systems deployed near infrastructure such as roads, power lines, or industrial equipment environmental and geophysical platforms that integrate seismic, muon, magnetic, or other sensing modalities detection systems that require high confidence in distinguishing real signatures from environmental noise These and related applications benefit from enhanced robustness and improved discrimination of true signals in field environments. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation
description: Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation from scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a cleaner, flexible way to capture and concentrate rare earth elements from complex liquid mixtures by using a bio-inspired protein system that gathers target metals into separable clusters. The approach is designed to reduce reliance on harsher processing methods while supporting more resilient supply chains for critical materials used across energy, electronics, transportation and advanced manufacturing markets. Because the system is genetically modular, the same platform may be adapted with different Lanmodulin-type metal-binding variants to support selective capture needs across varied feedstocks. How it Works The technology modifies Lanmodulin, a protein known for strong rare earth element binding, by adding an �encapsulation peptide" to the N-terminus of the protein. Once the engineered protein binds rare earth elements in solution, the resulting protein-metal complexes can be triggered for self-assemble into biomolecular condensates, which are larger clusters that can be removed from the liquid. The material can then be separated and concentrated through various means�such as centrifugation, filtration, and sedimentation�reducing the need for immobilizing the protein on a column or other fixed support. Technical Description Rare earth elements are important to modern technologies; yet, processing and purification can be difficult and environmentally damaging. Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation addresses that problem through EP-LanM, an engineered version of Lanmodulin that changes its material state when rare earth elements are present. Rather than focusing only on changing which rare earth elements Lanmodulin binds, this technology changes how the protein behaves after binding, turning dissolved protein-metal complexes into recoverable droplets. The metals can be harvested from the protein droplets, and the resultant free-protein itself can be recycled into iterative separations. The protein architecture is modular, with the encapsulation peptide fused to Lanmodulin so the protein can self-assemble in response to rare earth element binding. The assembled EP-LanM-rare earth complexes can be captured through simple centrifugation, filtration, or sedimentation, which may simplify processing compared with approaches that require immobilization on a column. The modular design may also support use with other Lanmodulin derivatives that have been designed for specific rare earth affinities, creating a path toward tailored separation strategies � without requiring a full redesign of the recovery concept. Advantages Uses a bio-based protein system for rare earth element capture Concentrates rare earth elements from complex mixtures Enables separation after droplet formation Avoids the need for protein immobilization in a column-based format Supports modular adaptation with different Lanmodulin derivatives Aligns with demand for more environmentally conscious critical-material recovery methods Allows recovery and recycling of input protein Market Applications Critical Minerals Recovery (rare earth concentration, mixed metal streams) Mining and Mineral Processing (process waters, low-grade sources) Waste Recycling (recovered components, mixed recycling streams) Environmental Remediation (metal-bearing waters, industrial residuals) Biomanufacturing and Bioseparation (engineered protein recovery tools, modular capture systems) Development Status: TRL 3 U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-25158 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: Accelerator-Driven Sub-Critical Molten-Salt Assembly (ADS+MSA Facility)
description: An accelerator-driven, sub-critical molten-salt nuclear system that centrally produces large quantities of tritium for fusion energy. By pairing accelerator-driven subcritical operation with molten-salt chemistry, the system offers a controllable, safety-forward pathway to produce fusion fuel, recover useful energy and convert legacy nuclear liabilities into strategic energy assets. Overview: The Accelerator-Driven Sub-Critical Molten-Salt Assembly (ADS+MSA) is a centralized nuclear facility that uses a high-power particle accelerator coupled to a liquid molten-salt system to reliably produce kilogram-scale quantities of tritium. Because the system is sub-critical, nuclear reactions only occur when driven by the accelerator, providing inherent safety and operational control. By combining proven accelerator technology with modern molten-salt chemistry, the ADS+MSA removes a major bottleneck to commercial fusion energy, recovers useful energy, and strengthens U.S. energy security and national security missions under existing Department of Energy safety frameworks rather than commercial reactor licensing. Key Advantages: Enables large-scale commercial fusion energy by providing a reliable, centralized source of tritium, eliminating the need for fusion plants to breed their own fuel and significantly reducing cost, complexity, and deployment risk. Operates in an inherently safe, sub-critical configuration in which nuclear reactions stop when the accelerator is turned off, avoiding runaway scenarios and allowing operation under DOE accelerator safety orders rather than NRC power-reactor licensing. Achieves extremely high tritium production efficiency, with tritium breeding ratios far exceeding those achievable in fusion reactor blankets, enabling kilogram-scale production with substantially lower accelerator power than earlier accelerator-only concepts. Builds on decades of proven accelerator development and growing industrial experience with molten-salt systems, reducing technical risk and enabling modular, scalable deployment as demand increases. Market Applications: Fusion Energy (fuel supply for commercial fusion power plants) Nuclear Waste Management (reduction and disposition of long-lived nuclear materials) Advanced Nuclear Energy (sub-critical and accelerator-driven nuclear systems) Government Nuclear Asset Management (utilization of surplus plutonium and uranium inventories) Industrial Energy and Infrastructure (on-site energy, heat, and supporting infrastructure) Clean Energy and Decarbonization (carbon-free baseload energy enablement) Development Status: TRL 3-4 IP Status: U.S. Patent pending LA-UR-26-25142 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: France – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Etude des schémas directeurs eaux usées et eaux pluviales Secteur 4
description: Le contrat porte sur les prestations suivantes : ETUDE DES SCHEMAS DIRECTEURS EAUX USEES ET EAUX PLUVIALES - SECTEUR 4 : La Plaine, La Romagne, Le Voide, Les Cerqueux, Nueil-sur-Layon, Saint-Hilaire-du-Bois, Saint-Léger-sous-Cholet, Somloire, Vihiers, Maulévrier Cholet Agglomération souhaite répondre aux enjeux et objectifs suivants : • évaluer la mise en œuvre des précédents schémas directeurs, en particulier sur le volet eaux usées, • atteindre 100 % de conformité des systèmes d’assainissement, • accompagner les projections d’urbanisation et d’aménagement du territoire traduites dans les zonages et le PLUi-H adopté en février 2026, • structurer et adapter la gestion des eaux pluviales urbaines dans une perspective durable et intégrée, • garantir la protection du milieu naturel, • anticiper l’évolution de la réglementation DERU 2 et du SDAGE 2028/2032, • disposer d’outils de gestions technique et économique du patrimoine qui définissent la planification des investissements et un programme précis de travaux à l’échelle intercommunale. Ainsi, l’étude s’appuiera sur les schémas directeurs précédents pour bâtir un nouveau plan pluriannuel d’investissement, à horizon 10 ans minimum, permettant de garantir le bon état de son patrimoine et son adéquation avec les évolutions urbaines, démographiques et économiques du territoire communautaire, ainsi que le respect des exigences réglementaires, la protection des milieux récepteurs, des biens et des personnes. A titre prévisionnel, les prestations devraient débuter en mars 2027, pour une durée maximum de 22 mois. Le marché est décomposé en 4 phases pour le schéma directeur eaux usées et 1 phase pour le schéma directeur eaux pluviales, définies comme suit : Schéma directeur eaux usées : Phase I : Etat des lieux et pré-diagnostic, Phase II : Recherche et caractérisation des eaux claires parasites et des surverses, Phase III : Modélisation, prospective, Phase IV : Bilan récapitulatif, étude de scénarios et élaboration du schéma directeur, Schéma directeur eaux pluviales : Phase I : Actualisation du bilan patrimonial et de la connaissance des dysfonctionnements. Durée Le marché prend effet à sa notification, et s'achève à l'issue de la dernière phase. Le délai d'exécution maximum du marché fixé par le maître d'ouvrage pour l’ensemble des phases est de 22 mois, hors période de validation.

Die Anlage umfasst mehrere Baukörper; Gegenstand des vorliegenden Projekts ist ausschliesslich das ehemalige Hotel- und Kongress- Gebäude. Das um 1975 erstellte Gebäude ist Teil eines Ensembles von regionaler Bedeutung und steht unter kantonalem Denkmalschutz. Nach einer Phase des teilweisen Leerstands wird das Gebäude instandgesetzt und einer neuen Nutzung zugeführt. Der grosse Saal bleibt für kulturelle und gesellschaftliche Veranstaltungen erhalten. Ergänzend entstehen Räumlichkeiten für Verwaltung, die allgemeine Musikschule sowie weitere Vereins- und Gemeinschafts- Nutzungen. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind die Schliessanlagen (BKP 275) für die Sanierung und Umnutzung des ehemaligen Hotel- und Kongressgebäudes. Der Auftrag umfasst die Lieferung und Montage der Schliessanlage einschliesslich der zugehörigen Komponenten sowie deren Einrichtung und Inbetriebnahme gemäss Ausschreibungsunterlagen und Leistungsverzeichnis. Dazu gehören die Abstimmung mit den beteiligten Gewerken an den Schnittstellen zu Türen und Zutrittskontrolle sowie sämtliche für die fachgerechte und funktionsfähige Ausführung erforderlichen Nebenleistungen. Das Gebäude befindet sich in einem innerörtlichen Umfeld. Während der Bauzeit ist auf die örtlichen Gegebenheiten, die Baustellenlogistik sowie auf Anwohner und angrenzende öffentliche Nutzungen besonders Rücksicht zu nehmen. Die detaillierte Beschreibung der Leistungen ist den Ausschreibungsunterlagen zu entnehmen.

description: Η παρούσα σύμβαση αφορά την παροχή υπηρεσιών περισυλλογής επιπλεόντων αντικειμένων και κηλίδων, καθώς και την αντιμετώπιση περιστατικών ρύπανσης από πετρέλαιο, άλλες ουσίες και φυσικοχημικά φαινόμενα (συμπεριλαμβανομένου του φυτοπλαγκτού) στον Θερμαϊκό Κόλπο. Συγκεκριμένα αφορά : Α) Την υπηρεσία καθαρισμού που καλύπτει τη γεωγραφική περιοχή από το Λιμάνι της Θεσσαλονίκης έως το Ακρωτήριο του Μεγάλου Εμβόλου (Αγία Τριάδα) στα ανατολικά, καθώς και τα Δέλτα των ποταμών Αξιού και Αλιάκμονα στα δυτικά. Β) Τη διαχείριση όλων των απορριμμάτων και κηλίδων που συλλέγονται, από το στάδιο της αρχικής συλλογής μέχρι το στάδιο της τελικής διάθεσης. Γ) Την υποβολή μηνιαίων εκθέσεων στις οποίες θα αναφέρονται οι εκτελεσθείσες κινήσεις και εργασίες ανά ημέρα, τα αποτελέσματα των εργασιών και τυχόν προβλήματα που παρουσιάστηκαν, φωτογραφικό υλικό από τις εκτελεσθείσες εργασίες και τις περιοχές εργασιών, τα είδη των συλλεχθέντων απορριμμάτων (ενδεικτικά: πλαστικό, γυαλί, μέταλλο, ξύλα, φυτικές ύλες) και έκτακτων περιστατικών ρύπανσης, τις συλλεχθείσες ποσότητες αποβλήτων ανά ημέρα εργασίας και συγκεντρωτικά ανά μήνα και τον χώρο τελικής διάθεσης αυτών. Οι παρεχόμενες υπηρεσίες κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων (CPV): 90733000-4 – «Υπηρεσίες που σχετίζονται με ρυπασμένα ύδατα». Η παρούσα σύμβαση δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα και ανατίθεται ως ενιαίο σύνολο, καθώς το φυσικό αντικείμενο είναι ενιαίο και αδιαίρετο και το έργο πρέπει να καταστεί εν το συνόλω λειτουργικό. Σε περίπτωση διαίρεσης σε τμήματα θα απαιτούνταν συντονισμός εργασιών προκειμένου να μην καταστεί η σύμβαση τεχνικά δύσκολη ή περαιτέρω δαπανηρή για την Αναθέτουσα Αρχή. Προσφορές υποβάλλονται για το σύνολο της σύμβασης. Η συνολική εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης για τη χρονική διάρκεια των δεκαοκτώ (18) μηνών ανέρχεται στο ποσό των διακοσίων εβδομήντα δύο χιλιάδων οκτακοσίων πενήντα ευρώ (272.850,00 €) μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ποσό με ΦΠΑ: 338.334,00 €). Η Αναθέτουσα Αρχή διατηρεί το Δικαίωμα Προαίρεσης για την ανάθεση πρόσθετων εργασιών τακτικού καθαρισμού και αντιμετώπισης φυτοπλαγκτού, συνολικού προϋπολογισμού έως 104.300,00 € μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ποσό με ΦΠΑ: 129.332,00 €). Ο συνολικός προϋπολογισμός της Διακήρυξης (συμπεριλαμβανομένου του Δικαιώματος Προαίρεσης) ανέρχεται στο ποσό των 377.150,00 € μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% (ποσό με ΦΠΑ 467.666,00 €). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης ορίζεται σε δεκαοχτώ (18) μήνες από την υπογραφή της και ειδικότερα από την ημερομηνία ανάρτησης στο ΚΗΜΔΗΣ. Η Αναθέτουσα Αρχή διατηρεί το δικαίωμα μονομερούς άσκησης προαίρεσης, συνολικής εκτιμώμενης αξίας 104.300,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ, υπό τους ίδιους όρους της αρχικής σύμβασης και σύμφωνα με τα αναλυτικά οριζόμενα στη Διακήρυξη, η οποία επιμερίζεται ως εξής: α) Για τους τακτικούς καθαρισμούς επιπλεόντων αντικειμένων: έως τριάντα (30) δυνητικά πρόσθετες ημέρες εργασίας (22 καθημερινές, 4 Σάββατα και 4 Κυριακές/αργίες), εκτιμώμενης αξίας 29.300,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ. β) Για τους έκτακτους καθαρισμούς φυτοπλαγκτού: έως πέντε (5) δυνητικά πρόσθετες επιχειρήσεις καθαρισμού, εκτιμώμενης αξίας 75.000,00 € πλέον ΦΠΑ.

title: Mittenza für Muttenz - maison de la culture Réaménagement et rénovation I BKP 275 Systèmes de fermeture
description:
La commune de Muttenz prévoit la rénovation et la réaffectation partielle d'un bâtiment existant à plusieurs étages, situé au sein du complexe « Mittenza », dans le centre historique. Le complexe comprend plusieurs corps de bâtiment ; le présent projet concerne exclusivement l'ancien bâtiment hôtelier et de congrès.

 

Construit vers 1975, ce bâtiment fait partie d'un ensemble d'importance régionale et est classé monument historique au niveau cantonal. Après une période de vacance partielle, l'édifice sera remis en état et affecté à de nouveaux usages. La grande salle sera conservée pour accueillir des événements culturels et sociaux. Par ailleurs, des espaces seront aménagés pour l'administration, l'école de musique, ainsi que pour diverses activités associatives et communautaires.

 

Le présent appel d'offres porte sur les systèmes de verrouillage (code CFC 275) dans le cadre de la rénovation et de la réaffectation de l'ancien bâtiment hôtelier et de congrès.

 

Le mandat comprend la fourniture et la pose du système de verrouillage, incluant les composants associés, ainsi que sa configuration et sa mise en service, conformément aux documents d'appel d'offres et au descriptif des prestations. Cela inclut la coordination avec les autres corps de métier aux interfaces avec les portes et les systèmes de contrôle d'accès, ainsi que toutes les prestations annexes nécessaires à une exécution conforme aux règles de l'art et garantissant le bon fonctionnement du système.

 

Le bâtiment est situé en milieu urbain dense. Durant la phase de travaux, une attention particulière devra être portée au contexte local, à la logistique du chantier, ainsi qu'aux riverains et aux espaces publics adjacents.

 

La description détaillée des prestations figure dans les documents d'appel d'offres.

description: Ruoveden kunta pyytää tarjousta omistamansa asuin- ja liikekiinteistö Säästökulman purku-urakasta tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Purkukohde sijaitsee osoitteessa Ruovedentie 36, 34600 Ruovesi. Urakka sisältää rakennuksen purkamisen kokonaisuudessaan, purkujätteen asianmukaisen lajittelun, käsittelyn ja poiskuljetuksen sekä purkamisen jälkeiset maanrakennus-, täyttö- ja maisemointityöt. Kohteen sisätiloissa suoritetaan parhaillaan erillinen asbestipurku ja siihen liittyvä siivous laittoman haitta-ainepurun seurauksena. Suoritettavien töiden yhteydessä sisätiloista poistetaan tiedossa olevat asbesti- ja haitta-ainepitoiset materiaalit. Rakennuksen perustuksissa, julkisivuissa sekä muissa rakenteissa saattaa kuitenkin edelleen esiintyä haitta-aineita sisältäviä materiaaleja. Kyseinen kohde sijaitsee noin 50 metrin etäisyydellä tästä purkukohteesta, ja kohteiden väliin jää yksi kiinteistö. Näiden materiaalien purkaminen, käsittely, pakkaaminen, kuljetus ja asianmukainen toimittaminen hyväksyttyyn vastaanottopaikkaan sisältyvät purku-urakkaan urakka-asiakirjoissa esitetyssä laajuudessa sekä voimassa olevien viranomaismääräysten mukaisesti. Tilaajalla on samanaikaisesti tarjouslaskennassa sisällöltään lähes vastaava purku-urakka. Kyseinen kohde sijaitsee noin 50 metrin etäisyydellä tästä purkukohteesta, ja kohteiden väliin jää yksi kiinteistö. Purkutyöt voidaan toteuttaa joko samanaikaisesti tai peräkkäin urakoitsijan tuotantosuunnittelun mukaisesti. Tarjoajaa pyydetään huomioimaan kyseinen mahdollinen synergiaetu tarjouslaskennassaan. Kohteet kilpailutetaan ja tilataan kuitenkin erillisinä toisistaan riippumattomina urakoina. Kumpaankin kohteeseen valitaan erikseen urakoitsija tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Valintaperusteena on hinnaltaan halvin hyväksyt-tävä tarjous. Tarjouspyyntödokumentti, soveltuvuusvaatimukset, hankinnan kohde ja tarkemmat hankinnan tiedot tutustuttavissa latauslinkin takaa. title: APN - Ramp B East Replacement Project 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE Ramp B East Replacement Project 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 15 Wing Moose Jaw. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES CFB 15 Wing Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, requires the repair and replacement of the existing Ramp B East at the airbase.The Department of National Defence and Defence Construction Canada intends to put in place a contract to provide all labour, materials, and equipment for work including, but not necessarily limited to, the following:    Installation of temporary security fencing and construction barriers  Demolition and removal of existing concrete pavement  Partial removal of existing granular base  Topsoil stripping and stockpiling  Grading and compaction of the existing granular base and placement of new granular base  Construction of new Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavements  Installation of new joint sealant and paint markings  Landscaping, including topsoil, fertilizer, and hydroseeding  It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. Contract Number: CN88327 Title: Ramp B East Replacement Project , 15 Wing, Moose Jaw, SK Approximate Estimate: $16,000,000 Anticipated Posting: January 2027 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a tenderer will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS) 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a tender for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential tenderers with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a tender.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a tender will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the tenderer will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Wiley Reid Team Leader, Programs Defence Construction Canada 306-513-5681 Wiley.Reid@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the tenderer agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the tenderer for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sponsorship process.Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. title: Rénovation complète (rénovation technique) de la « Freidbad-Seebad » de Spiez – Mandataire général
description: La commune de Spiez envisage de procéder à une rénovation (technique) complète de la piscine en plein air construite en 1979 et 1980 dans la baie de Spiez. Le complexe comprend un bassin de 50 mètres, un bassin de plongeon équipé de plongeoirs de 1 m et 3 m, un bassin pour non-nageurs, une pataugeoire pour enfants ainsi qu'un toboggan aquatique. Depuis la construction des installations, diverses adaptations et rénovations ont été effectuées, mais un besoin important de rénovation se fait désormais sentir. Les revêtements des bassins ont atteint la fin de leur cycle de vie après environ 25 ans, les équipements techniques, dont certains datent de la construction, ont plus de 45 ans, et le toboggan aquatique de 1998 doit parfois être étanchéifié chaque année. Il s’agit d’une rénovation de l’infrastructure de baignade, y compris des composants techniques, mais pas d’un réaménagement du complexe ni de la rénovation des bâtiments.
