title: Electrical Brush
description: DLA Weapons Support - Richmond is issuing this source sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for the following: NSN 5977-00-311-6328 Sources: National Electrical Carbon (CAGE 0VJZ4) P/N 36A164453BCP01 The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 335991 THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements; 3) implement a successful project management plan that includes: compliance with tight program schedules; cost containment; meeting and tracking performance; hiring and retention of key personnel and risk mitigation; and 4) provide services under a performance based service acquisition contract. BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above-listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice by Dec 23, 2025 @ 2:00 pm EST. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to cassandra.cooper@dla.mil If you have any questions concerning this opportunity, please contact: Cassandra Cooper Email: cassandra.cooper@dla.mil APPENDIX 1: Purpose and Objectives Potential sources shall be capable of furnishing all labor, materials, facilities and equipment required to accomplish the new manufacture of the item(s). Generally, this entails the procurement/manufacture of component parts, inspection, testing, preservation/packaging, and shipping. Additionally, potential sources may be responsible for supply chain management, logistics planning, forecasting production requirements, long-lead time parts procurement, diminishing manufacturing sources and material shortage issues, and shipping serviceable assets. The unit prices will be established at the time of a contract award. Technical Orders and Qualification Requirements are not available.

title: 2930-014332550, cooler, lubricating oil, engine
description: SYNOPSIS / PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE DLA Weapons Support-Columbus anticipates issuing Solicitation SPE7MX-27-R-X003 for the establishment of a Long-Term Contract (LTC) utilizing the commercial item procedures of FAR Part 12.201-1. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity Contract (IDIQ) with a five-year ordering period consisting of a three-year base period and two one-year option periods. This acquisition will support continued and improved supply availability for a critical DLA-managed item. This procurement is being conducted as Other than Full and Open Competition. The Government reserves the right to make award on a Best Value basis. While price may be a significant evaluation factor, award may be made to an offeror other than the lowest-priced offeror after consideration of factors including, but not limited to, price, past performance, delivery performance, and other evaluation criteria identified in the solicitation. Item Description: CLIN 0001 NSN: 2930-014332550 Nomenclature: cooler, lubricating oil, engine Approved Source Item Export Control Applies Contractor First Article Test (FAT) Requirement Applies Surge Requirements Apply Contract Requirements: Inspection and Acceptance: Origin FOB: Source Requested Delivery: 90 Days After Receipt of Order (ARO) once FAT approved Technical Data: This project contains source-controlled drawings/specifications. You may access them through the following link: https://tdmt.dla.mil. Drawings are available directly from TDMT by querying for MR014332550 in the Solicitation field. Trade Agreements / Domestic Preference: One or more of the items under this acquisition may be subject to an Agreement on Government Procurement approved and implemented in the United States by the Trade Agreements Act of 1979. All offers shall be in the English language and in U.S. dollars. The solicitation will identify all applicable domestic preference and trade agreement provisions. All interested suppliers may submit a quotation. Delivery Requirements: Shipping instructions will be provided on individual delivery orders. Material ordered under the resulting contract shall be delivered within 140 days after receipt of each delivery order. Notwithstanding any other provision of the contract, no deliveries shall be made prior to issuance of a delivery order (DD Form 1155). Solicitation Availability: A copy of the solicitation will be available on 11/23/2026 via the DLA Internet Bid Board System at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil. Choose the DLA Request for Proposals (RFP) / Invitation for Bid (IFB) option under Solicitations. Enter the solicitation number within the search value area and click the submit button. Solicitations are in Portable Document Format (PDF). To download and view these documents, use the latest version of Adobe Acrobat Reader. This software is available free at http://www.adobe.com. A paper copy of the solicitation may be provided to requestors on a case-by-case basis if access to DIBBS is not available. Proposal Submission: DIBBS quotations are acceptable for this solicitation. Offerors are responsible for completing the solicitation in its entirety. The preferred method of submission is via upload through DIBBS. Alternatively, offers may be submitted electronically to: Mandy Phipps-Kuhlman Email: mandy.phipps-kuhlman@dla.mil Offerors submitting proposals outside of DIBBS shall submit a completed and signed SF 1449, Request for Quote (RFQ), in electronic PDF format prior to closing date and time listed in the solicitation. This notice does not constitute a contract or a commitment of any kind by the Government. The Government reserves the right to cancel this acquisition at any time for a SAM.gov pre-solicitation notice. Additional Information: NAICS Code: 336310 FSC: 2930 AMC/AMSC: 3/B Estimated Annual Demand Quantity (ADQ): 162 EA FAT Schedule: 90 Days FAT Report Submission / 60 Days Government Evaluation

title: RFI - Novel or Multifunctional Fibers, Yarns, Coatings/Finishes and Fabrics for Soldier Protection and Comfort (MFFYF)
description: SYNOPSIS: This Sources Sought Announcement is to assist the US Army DEVCOM Soldier Center, in coordination with the Product Manager for Soldier Clothing and Individual Equipment (PdM SCIE), to identify potential sources of multifunctional fibers, yarns, fabrics, coatings, or finishes for Soldier protection, thermal comfort and/or physical comfort. The RFI is issued for the purpose of identifying and assessing novel fibers, yarns, fabrics, coatings or finishes. Of primary interest are multifunctional submissions that provide at least two (2) functionalities (e.g., a moisture management fiber knit into a vector protective structure, an oil repellant coating or finish applied to flame resistant fabric). The Government seeks both near- and far-term approaches: Near-Term Solutions (TRL 5�7+): Mature, drop-in, or near-term standalone textile solutions that can be rapidly validated by DEVCOM SC and could be inserted into active military Programs of Record (PORs). Near-term solutions should be able to withstand laundering and abrasion while maintaining functionality. Far-Term Next-Generation Concepts (TRL 2�4): Emerging, exploratory concepts (e.g., novel fiber cross-sections, grooved/star-shaped capillaries, re-entrant geometries, mechanical vector-barrier architectures, vector protective chemistries, biomimetic moisture channels, and advanced microclimate finishes) to inform technology investments for future uniform platforms. The RFI is issued solely for information gathering and planning purposes. The RFI does not constitute a formal solicitation for proposals and will not directly lead to any contract awards. The following sections of this announcement contain details of the scope of technical interest as well as instructions for submitting a response. The Government requests that responses be submitted electronically to paola.a.dangelo.civ@army.mil and joseph.a.orlando38.civ@army.mil by 23 December 2026 by 5pm EST. Background: This RFI is intended to identify products and suppliers that provide textile multifunctionality to enhance the environmental protection of dismounted Warfighters. Dismounted Warfighters are often exposed to rapid shifts between extreme physical exertion (producing high metabolic sweat and vapor) and prolonged static postures (firing in the prone, kneeling on sub-zero surfaces, sitting in observation posts/foxholes). Protection against extreme environmental conditions (cold or hot, wet or dry) and the compounding physiological stresses induced by their specific mission profiles, equipment loads, and operational postures is desired. title: PACA Special Audits RFQ
description: General The Air Force Services Center (AFSVC), headquartered at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland, Texas, delivers Services programs and activities to build and sustain ready and resilient Airmen, Guardians, and families. Air Force Services Center supports bases, major commands (MAJCOMs), and the Air Staff by providing technical expertise, launching new initiatives, developing programs and operational procedures, and managing central support functions. Air Force Services Center ensures the successful operation of essential food services, fitness and sports centers, childcare and youth programs, lodging accommodations, and recreational opportunities for military members and their families worldwide. The Center�s responsibilities include preparing responses to high-level inquiries, providing technical assistance to the field, and developing new programs supporting installation activities. The Financial Management Directorate (VF) centrally manages and administers the Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) Public Accountant Contract Audit (PACA) Program, which supports a worldwide mission providing independent oversight of internal controls, cash management, asset protection, and financial management across the enterprise. Background Nonappropriated Fund (NAF) installations provide support services and activities for military personnel, families, and authorized patrons. Proper management and accountability of Nonappropriated Fund resources are critical to ensuring continued service delivery, operational readiness, and the protection of government interests. Regular independent audits are required to evaluate the financial condition, control environments, and operational efficiencies of Nonappropriated Fund operations. The Air Force Services Center Financial Management, Strategic Policy & Financial Operations Branch (AFSVC/VFSF) exercises central program oversight to ensure compliance with annual statutory audit requirements under Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 7600.06, Audit of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities and Related Activities, ensuring adequate audit coverage is provided across the enterprise for Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) Services activities. The term "Activities" refers to operational and revenue-generating entities within the Air Force structure. Audit engagements under this Special Audits contract specifically include financial statement audits and performance audits covering: � Accounting practices and transactional compliance; � Internal control environments and segregation of duties; � Cash management, vault operations, and electronic banking; � Fixed asset accountability, tracking, and depreciation; � Inventory valuation, spoilage controls, and physical counts; � Food and beverage operations and food service portfolios; � Centralized shared service center processing; � Venture gaming and electronic slot machine operations; � Supplemental mission dining operations; and � Agreed-upon procedures and special interest compliance reviews. Specific Focus Areas for the PACA Special Audits Program: � A. Shared Service Center (SSC): Conduct performance audits of the Shared Service Center (SSC) at the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC) located in San Antonio, TX. The primary objective of the performance audit is to address economy, efficiency, and operational effectiveness. The scope includes core accounting transaction workflows, inter-entity cost allocation methodologies, compliance with Service Level Agreements (SLAs), operational metrics, and the adequacy of financial management technology system controls. Further details will be outlined in specific delivery order project assignments. � B. Department of the Air Force (DAF) Venture Gaming Program: The DAF Venture Gaming Program operates electronic gaming and slot machine activities at authorized overseas military installations. The program serves as an important nonappropriated revenue generator utilized directly to support and enhance Morale, Welfare, and Recreation (MWR) programs across all Air Force installations. Authorized by DoDI 1015.10 and centrally managed by AFSVC in San Antonio, TX, slot machine operations present unique risks due to regulatory complexities, high cash volumes, and potential for manipulation. Scope includes electronic gaming data systems, meter reconciliations, cash drop and count controls, payout authorizations, jackpot disbursements, internal control safeguards against manipulation or theft, and compliance with federal tax reporting requirements (including IRS Form W-2G processing). � C. Air Force Cadet Dining Fund: The Cadet Dining Fund is a Supplemental Mission Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) operated by the 10th Force Support Squadron (10th FSS) located at the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA), Colorado. Supplemental Mission NAFIs receive nonappropriated funds generated from installation mission programs (training, food service, education, security). While congressionally appropriated funds (APF) cover civilian management, custodial services, and facility upkeep, nonappropriated funds are utilized strictly for food purchases and the operational maintenance of cadet meal operations. The fund provides daily dining support for over 4,400 cadets. The Contractor shall perform comprehensive financial statement and operational compliance audits examining food supply procurement, inventory receiving and storage controls, cost-per-meal accounting, meal card verifications, and financial statement accuracy in accordance with USAFAI 34-104 and applicable NAF regulations. � D. Commander�s Special Interest Audits: To address immediate, unplanned operational needs, the Government requires the capacity to execute ad hoc, targeted investigations known as Commander�s Special Interest Audits. These audits may be requested at any given time by Installation Commanders, the AFSVC Commander, or higher headquarters to address immediate operational concerns, suspected material control failures, or strategic risk areas. These ad hoc engagements may encompass any Air Force Installation, NAF Activity, or fund within the scope of this contract, and will be ordered and executed as individual, consolidated performance audit task orders in accordance with the established deliverables and pricing schedules. Scope Air Force Services Center requires the audit services of licensed Certified Public Accountants (CPAs) or CPA firms to perform financial statement audits of Air Force Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentalities (NAFIs) financial statements and performance audits of Nonappropriated Fund Instrumentality (NAFI) Services activities, with particular emphasis on high-risk areas identified through preliminary risk assessments and annual selection matrices.

The Regional Water Supply St. Gallen (RWSG) is currently constructing the new Riet II lakewater plant. buyer: Office fédéral des constructions et de la logistique OFCL
title: (b26012-8) Rénovation et agrandissement des serres d’Agroscope à Reckenholz / CFC 231
description:
Agroscope, le centre de compétence de la Confédération pour la recherche agronomique, planifie son futur centre de recherche de Reckenholz en s’appuyant sur les installations existantes. L’infrastructure en place doit être adaptée aux nouvelles exigences en plusieurs étapes, au moyen de transformations et de rénovations.

Une partie des serres et des installations du bâtiment d’exploitation ont atteint la fin de leur cycle de vie. La rénovation se déroulera en deux étapes. Lors de la première, certaines serres seront remplacées par des chambres de recherche entièrement fermées et climatisées. En outre, le bâtiment d’exploitation sera rénové et agrandi, et les installations seront adaptées aux nouvelles exigences. Les autres serres seront remplacées lors de la deuxième étape.

Le présent appel d’offres concerne uniquement la première étape. Pendant la durée des travaux de construction, les autres serres resteront en exploitation.

title: Tender BKP 248.2 Cold Rooms
description:
Project Summary:


A new care center is to be constructed on plot no. 7297 for the company "Wohnen und Pflege Peteracker AG." The project comprises 56 care rooms and associated ancillary spaces, distributed across three floors. The ground floor will house a dedicated unit for residents with dementia, as well as a public restaurant and a dining hall for residents.


1. Background

In light of the constantly evolving and complex requirements for modern retirement and nursing homes—and for forward-looking elderly care—the Social Services Authority initiated the "Vision for Aging and Strategy for the Peteracker Retirement and Nursing Home (APH)" project in the autumn of 2017. The project focused on two main areas: inpatient care (at the Peteracker Retirement and Nursing Home, APH) and services for seniors who do not require inpatient care. The "Vision for Aging and Strategy for the Peteracker Retirement and Nursing Home (APH)" project was designed to be flexible enough to address both current and future requirements.

On February 13, 2022, the municipality’s electorate approved the separation of the Peteracker Retirement and Nursing Home (APH) from the political municipality of Rafz, transitioning it into a non-profit public limited company.

The Peteracker APH currently provides a living environment for 42 residents, offering high-quality, needs-based care and support, along with a range of other services. It is the only institution of its kind in the municipality of Rafz. "Wohnen und Pflege Peteracker AG" operates the retirement and nursing home and has acquired the land from the municipality under a long-term leasehold agreement (building rights). The Peteracker site, home to the Peteracker retirement and nursing home (APH), is located just outside the village center of Rafz, situated between the main road and the SBB railway line. Directly opposite the Peteracker facility lies the former brickworks of the Zürcher Ziegeleien (Zurich Brickworks). The area is defined by a distinct rural charm.


2. Urban Design

The new building integrates into the existing Peteracker complex as part of a hamlet-like ensemble. Its positioning takes its cue from the loose arrangement of the existing structures, strengthening their spatial cohesion. The substantial building mass is articulated through a longitudinal main structure and two flanking wings; this gives the impression of a composition of smaller building volumes, remaining in keeping with the local scale. At the center, a new, courtyard-like village square emerges, serving as a communal space that fosters a sense of identity. Visual connections to the open landscape and the existing buildings are preserved.


3. Functional Distribution

The ground floor serves as the public hub of the facility, housing the entrance, reception, restaurant, and dining hall. These spaces are designed for flexible use and can be combined to accommodate events. The administrative offices are directly connected to the entrance area, while the kitchen, delivery, and logistics zones are functionally organized with separate access. The upper floors contain four residential units, comprising a total of 44 single rooms. Each unit is clearly laid out and accessible via a circular circulation path. A specialized residential unit for 13 residents with dementia is located in a protected setting on the raised ground floor, with direct access to a private garden. The basement level houses the laundry facility, as well as storage and technical areas. It also contains an underground parking garage with 24 spaces for the care center’s staff.


4. Landscape Design

The landscape at the edge of the settlement in the Rafzerfeld region combines a high quality of rural life with an environment shaped by a cultivated landscape. The open-space concept draws upon the loosely arranged structure typical of the local area, developing the site into a hamlet-like complex centered around a village square. Green spaces and plantings structure the outdoor area, minimize sealed surfaces, and integrate the site into the surrounding landscape. A sophisticated network of paths, combined with a clear separation between vehicular and pedestrian traffic, ensures excellent accessibility and a high-quality environment for spending time outdoors. Furthermore, specific features—such as a south-facing sun terrace, a sheltered garden for residents with dementia, and a diverse range of plantings—create attractive spaces that enhance the well-being of the residents.


5. Construction

The building’s structural framework is composed of reinforced concrete and masonry. Seismic safety is ensured through continuous circulation cores spanning all floors, strategically placed concrete shear walls within the exterior envelope, and reinforced concrete floor slabs. The building’s exterior walls consist of non-load-bearing, insulated timber elements that span multiple floors. On the interior, these elements are fitted with a service layer for building installations, while the exterior is clad in a ventilated timber façade.

title: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Mission Training Complex (MTC)
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. This synopsis is hereby issued in accordance with FAR Part 5.203, to announce the Government's intent to award a 8-month, Firm Fixed-Price Bridge Contract, on a noncompetitive basis to Trideum Corporation (CAGE 351S9) for the Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Mission Training Complex Capabilities Support (MTCCS) effort. This is a notice of intent to award a sole source contract under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(l) set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement Procedures, Guidance, and Information 206-302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Army Contracting Command-Orlando (ACC-ORL} and JBSA have identified a need to award a sole source contract to Trideum Corp (CAGE 351S9), to continue performance of JBSA MTCCS requirements. The current JBSA MTCCS Task Order expires 28 JAN 26. The contemplated sole source contract will include a limited performance period of five (5) months, commencing 29 JAN 2026 - 30 SEP 2026, ensuring continuation of mission command (MC) training at the JBSA Mission Training Complexes (MTCs). Services performed under this sole source contract will include the continuation of non-personal services to support the Mission Training Complex (MTC) to units stationed at and supported by Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA). No other contractor is in the position to assemble a large team of administrative, program management and subject matter experts (SMEs) who specialize in providing individual through collective Mission Command (MC} training, by the expiration of the current JBSA MTCCS contract performance period (28 JAN 26}. Award to anyone other than the incumbent contractor (Trideum) would result in a significant break in service. Award of this limited Bridge Contract is result of decrements identified in the Program Objective Memorandum for Fiscal Years FY27 through FY31 (POM 27-31), and as a result, the JBSA MTC will close at the end of FY26. This is NOT a request for competitive quotes. The Government intends to negotiate solely under statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 2304(c}(l) set forth in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1. Any interested firms must identity their interest and capability to respond to the requirement no later than 15 business days after this notice posts. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Please respond by 24 DEC 2025 at 1300 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST). Your response must include your stated technical knowledge of and experience with mission command (MC) training and information to demonstrate the Contractor's ability to complete Phase-In activities and commence full performance by the end of the current JBSA contract (28 JAN 2026). Send your response to Will Bass via willie.c.bass2.civ@army.mil. All responding contractors must be registered to the System for Award Management (SAM).

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos and Thermo RSLCnano UPLC Maintenance Agreement
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention intends to award a sole source firm fixed price purchase order to Thermo Electron North America LLC for an annual maintenance agreement for a mass spectrometer (Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos) and attached nano-UPLC system (Thermo RSLCnano UPLC). Thermo Electron North America LLC is the only vendor available that can provide service and maintenance for these instruments, which are highly complex and have many proprietary parts manufactured and sold exclusive by them. Unity Labs is the service branch of Thermo Electron North America. Only Unity service engineers have access to the training and parts needed to maintain the instruments at the required service levels. The anticipated period of performance is January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028. This contract action is for supplies or services for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b) (SAP) and 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1). Interested vendors may identify their interest and capability to respond to the requirement or submit proposals. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, all quotations/responses received within fifteen (15) days of the issuance of this notice will be considered by the government. A determination by the government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Any quotation/response should be emailed to the Contracting Officer, Denedra Hardy, at qfa5@cdc.gov by December 24, 2025.

title: INDUSTRY DAY: WPC Work Platforms
description: INDUSTRY DAY: Department of Homeland Security, United States Coast Guard (USCG), Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), CG Yard Location: USCG Yard, 2401 Hawkins Point Rd, Baltimore MD 21226 Description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an Industry Day event on 08 January 2026 at 9:00am ET. All interested parties are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view the registration information, attachments, and details below. The USCG plans to conduct a multi-phased approach to market research including: 1) requesting submission of capabilities statement, 2) an in-person industry day, and 3) one-on-one engagements with industry. The U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) will be holding an Industry Day event to engage with industry about the USCG�s needs relating to a potential upcoming requirement(s) and obtain information from industry as the USCG continues to seek a system of work platforms to facilitate exterior hull preservation on the 154� WPC Fast Response Cutter. The USCG will share more information about the scope of the requirements, the challenges we have identified, and the goals of the program. The venue has a capacity limitation; therefore, each vendor is limited to two participants. To participate, vendors should email Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist). All responses are due no later than 26 December 2025 at 4:00pm EST. The in-person Industry Day presentation will be recorded and or transcribed and publicly posted.? This is a follow-on to the USCG�s previously published Request for Information (RFI) that preliminarily describes the USCG�s needs. The previously published RFI (70Z04026RFI62204Y00) is attached to this Special Notice for reference purposes. INDUSTRY DAY AND ONE-ON-ONE SESSIONS GENERAL Industry Day The USCG will host an Industry Day on 08 January 2026, from 9:00am � 11:30am ET. A finalized agenda for the event will be sent out by 02 January 2026. In preparation for the in-person Industry Day, USCG asks interested vendors to review the information provided in the appendices and submit questions to Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist), so the USCG can be prepared to share the questions received and the answers. Please be advised that all questions and answers will be shared publicly. Therefore, interested parties are encouraged not to submit proprietary information with their questions. One-on-One Sessions The one-on-one engagements with vendors will occur immediately following the in-person industry day on 08 January 2026. Vendors should express their interest in a one-on-one session when registering via email. The USCG will follow up, no later than 02 January 2026, with a scheduled time for one-on-one engagements. There will be approximately 8 time slots available for one-on-one sessions. Each appointment is limited to approximately 15 minutes. Your confirmed one-on-one time will be included as a follow-on email to your registration confirmation. The purpose of these one-on-one sessions is to gather objective feedback, foster open dialogue, and obtain information from industry as the USCG continues to seek a system of work platforms to facilitate exterior hull preservation on the 154� WPC Fast Response Cutter. [YA1] [LL2] This will provide interested vendors with an opportunity to share potential proprietary solutions/services information for consideration and allow the Government to ask the vendor specific questions. These sessions are not a platform for vendor promotion. NOTE: Please be advised that if your company has already submitted questions regarding the requirements in response to our previous Request for Information (RFI), these questions will be addressed on SAM.gov, with select questions discussed during the Industry Day. All questions will be answered by the date the Industry Day recording is posted. Registration If your company plans on attending the General Session of the Industry Day and/or scheduling an appointment for a One-on-One session, please email Linda.B.Lassiter@uscg.mil (Contract Specialist) no later than 26 December 2025 at 4:00pm EST. If requesting to schedule an appointment for a one-on-one session, please be sure to request it at this time. The Government will follow up no later than 02 January 2026 with a scheduled time for one-on-one engagements. Under the direction of building owners, the Federal Protective Service will ensure that all entrants meet the necessary entry requirements. Upon arrival, individuals may be asked to present a REAL ID-compliant driver�s license, passport, or other acceptable ID (https://www.tsa.gov/travel/securityscreening/identification). This change is designed to enhance security while establishing consistent identification standards across federal facilities nationwide. description: ATVIRAS PROJEKTO KONKURSAS. Tauralaukio rajono teritorijos, pagal Klaipėdos miesto bendrojo plano sprendinius patenkančios į 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.8 ir 9.9 nagrinėjamus rajonus, urbanistinės idėjos atviras projekto konkursas. Projekto konkurso tikslas - išrinkti geriausiai urbanistinius, architektūros ir funkcinius aspektus bei kitus reikalavimus, išvardintus konkurso sąlygose, atitinkančią Tauralaukio rajono teritorijos, pagal Klaipėdos miesto bendrojo plano sprendinius patenkančios į 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.8 ir 9.9 nagrinėjamus rajonus, urbanistinės idėjos projektą, kurio pagrindu ateityje bus rengiami teritorijų planavimo dokumentai ir vystoma ši Tauralaukio rajono teritorija. Biudžetas: šio projekto konkurso pirkimo objekto įgyvendinimui (t.y. urbanistinės koncepcijos parengimui) suplanuota suma - 50 000 Eur su PVM (41 322,31 Eur be PVM). Vadovaujantis VPĮ 55 str. 3 d. Perkančioji organizacija konkurso dokumentuose iš anksto nustato fiksuotą kainą projekto konkurso pirkimo objekto įgyvendinimui (t.y. urbanistinės koncepcijos parengimui) - 50 000 Eur su PVM (arba 41 322,31 Eur be PVM, jei tiekėjas yra ne PVM mokėtojas ar paslaugos neapmokestinamos PVM, ar dėl kitų priežasčių, dėl kurių Perkančiosios organizacijos galutinė tiekėjui mokėtina suma bus be PVM). Projekto konkurso pirmąsias 3 vietas užėmusius dalyvius numatyta apdovanoti piniginiais prizais (premijomis), skiriant 40 000 Eur, prizinį fondą išskirstant tokia seka: I vieta – 16 000 Eur; II vieta – 14 000 Eur; III vieta – 10 000 Eur. Perkančioji organizacija laimėjusiu nustato tik 1 (vieną) dalyvį, surinkusį daugiausiai balų ir esantį pirmoje vietoje, neatitikusį pašalinimo pagrindų ir atitikusį nustatytus kvalifikacijos reikalavimus. Su projekto konkurso laimėtoju numatoma sudaryti paslaugų pirkimo–pardavimo sutartį dėl urbanistinės koncepcijos parengimo.

title: Norway – Internal audit services – Internal Audit Services
description: 1. Purpose and agreement period 1.1 Purpose The contract shall ensure NTNU access to independent, objective and risk based internal audit services of high professional quality. The internal audit shall contribute to strengthen NTNU ́s performance management, risk management and internal control and give the board an independent basis for assessment and follow-up. The agreement shall facilitate for continuity, good business understanding and a long-term cooperation, at the same time that the audit work shall be able to be adapted to changes in NTNU ́s risk picture, business and priorities. 2. Content of the Service 2.1 General The tenderer shall provide an overall internal audit service that includes: Preparation of annual risk based audit plan. Implementation of internal audits within the approved audit plan. Reporting audit results, findings and recommendations. Follow-up of measures after completed audits. Consultancy services for performance management, risk management and internal control within the limits of the independence of the internal audit. Ongoing dialogue with relevant parts of NTNU's management and organisation. Reporting to the board and other relevant decision-making bodies. Tenderers shall carry out the assignments with due diligence, objectivity and quality, in accordance with Global Standards for Internal Audit (GIAS) set by The Institute of Internal Auditors, in the at any given time applicable version, and NTNU ́s instructions for internal audits. If an assignment cannot be carried out in accordance with GIAS, the tenderer shall provide information on this in the report, stating which standards have not been followed, the reason and consequences for observations and conclusions. Special audits or surveys shall be possible if there is a need that is not included in the annual audit plan. 2.2 NTNU ́s guidelines The guidelines are attached. The version of the instructions that apply when the contract is signed, is dated 29 April 2018. October 2020. NTNU can update the guidelines during the agreement period. Changes that do not significantly affect the tenderer's obligations shall be followed within the agreed remuneration. 2.3 Annual risk assessment and audit plan Tenderers shall annually carry out a general risk assessment of NTNU ́s activities and prepare a justified proposal for the audit plan with the hourly budget for the coming years. The risk assessment shall be based on the understanding of NTNU's social mission, organisation, strategic aims and framework conditions. Tenderers shall obtain and assess relevant information from i.a. the board, university management, risk assessments, previous audits and other relevant sources. The tenderer shall justify the priorities. It shall be clear what risks the audits are meant to highlight, and what significant risks are not prioritised and why. The audit plan shall be processed and approved by NTNU's board of directors in accordance with the current management scheme. 2.4 Implementation of audits Each audit shall be planned and carried out based on an approved audit plan. After each audit, the tenderer shall prepare a report that is clear and relevant for decision making. Finds and recommendations shall be prioritised in accordance with materiality and risk. The principal shall continuously receive audit reports from the individual audits. The results of the audit activities performed shall be reported half yearly to the board. Serious conditions shall be reported at the first possible board meeting. The biannual reports shall mention completed audits, significant findings, status for follow-up of measures and any overall developments. 2.5 Follow-up and advice Consultancy shall be carried out in a way that safeguards the independence of internal audits. Tenderers shall not take over NTNU ́s management responsibility or decision authority.

title: Czechia – Intercity railway works – „Revitalizace trati Kostelec – Telč – Slavonice, 1. etapa“
description: Předmětem této veřejné zakázky „Revitalizace trati Kostelec – Telč – Slavonice, 1. etapa“ je: a) Zhotovení Projektové dokumentace pro provádění stavby dráhy (PDPS) v režimu BIM, která rozpracuje a vymezí požadavky na stavbu do podrobností, které specifikují předmět Díla se zohledněním konkrétních výrobků, dodávaných technologií, technologických postupů a výrobních podmínek Zhotovitele stavby, včetně posouzení shody nebo vhodnosti pro použití prvku interoperability či ES prohlášení o ověření subsystému oznámeným subjektem. b) Zpracování Díla v režimu BIM a vytvoření Informačního modelu BIM podle SOD Přílohy č. 10 BIM protokol, včetně všech jeho příloh. Informační model je součást Díla a bude zpracováván, projednáván a odevzdáván průběžně a společně s ostatními části Díla. c) Výkon Dozoru projektanta při provádění stavby d) Zhotovení stavby dle schválené Projektové dokumentace a pravomocného povolení záměru (povolení stavby). Investiční akce bude rozdělena do samostatných etap (zakázek), směřujících k postupnému dosažení cíle. Jedná se o etapy: • Revitalizace trati Kostelec – Telč – Slavonice, kácení (dále jen „Kácení“), • Revitalizace trati Kostelec – Telč – Slavonice, 1. etapa (D+B) (dále jen „1. etapa“), • Revitalizace trati Kostelec – Telč – Slavonice, 2. a 3. etapa (DPS+PDPS) (dále jen „2. etapa“). title: NATO Business Opportunity: Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) Tactical Battle Management (TBM) Capabilities
description: The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) intends to issue a solicitation for the provision of a Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) Tactical Battle Management (TBM) System including In-Service Support and Enhancements. Potential U.S. prime contractors must 1) maintain a professionally active facility (office, factory, laboratory, etc.) within the United States, 2) hold a Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the level of SECRET or higher, 3) be pre-approved for participation in NATO Competitive Procurement (NCP), 4) be issued a Declaration of Eligibility (DOE) by the Department of Commerce (DOC), and 5) register with NCIA�s eProcurement tool, Neo: https://www.ncia.nato.int/business/procurement/neo-eprocurement Pre-competitive Industry Engagement will take place in the form of a BMD TBM Workshop at NATO Edge, taking place on 17-19 November in Izmir, T�rkiye. Please see the attached Calling Notice for details. More information on NATO Edge attendance and registration is available on event�s official website -https://www.natoedge.nato.int/. For those who cannot attend NATO Edge, a pre-competitive Request for Information is included in the second attachment. Submit responses via the email address in the attachment no later than 12:00 hours Central European Time (CET) on 03 December 2026. The reference for the solicitation is CCO-423316-RTBMD and all correspondence concerning the solicitation should include this reference. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT Please see attached. BECOMING ELIGIBLE TO BID NCP requires that the U.S. Government issue a DOE for potential U.S. prime contractors interested in this project. Before the U.S. Government can do so, however, the U.S. Government must approve the U.S. firm for participation in NCP. U.S. firms are approved for NCP on a facility-by-facility basis. The U.S. NCP application is a one-time application. The application requires supporting documentation in the form of 1) a company resume or capability statement indicating contracts completed as a prime contractor and 2) an annual report or set of financial documents indicating compilation, review, or audit by an independent CPA. The U.S. Government continues to accept the legacy NATO International Competitive Bidding (ICB) application for participation in NCP. U.S. firms can download a copy of the legacy ICB application from the following website: https://www.bis.gov/about-bis/bis-leadership-and-offices/SIES/business-opportunities-nato DOC is the U.S. Government agency that approves NCP applications. Please submit to the email address provided your application and supporting documentation (as attachments). If your firm is interested in a specific NCP project at this time, please also include the following in the TEXT of your email: - the title and/or solicitation number of the project - the name/phone/email of the company employee who should receive the bid documents After approval of your one-time NCP application, DOC will then know to follow up by issuing a DOE for the project. DOC will transmit the DOE to the NATO contracting agency. title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Clobazam, (OBG) ATC N05BA09 für die Zeit 01.03.2025 - 28.02.2027
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff, Clobazam, ATC N05BA09, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.03.2025 in Kraft und endet am 28.02.2027. Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.

In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff, Telmisartan + Amlodipin, ATC C09DB04, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.03.2025 in Kraft und endet am 28.02.2027. Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.
